root.name: Sicilian Defense: Delayed Alapin Variation, with e6

overview: White plays the Alapin plan of c3 and d4 after 2...e6. The main reply is 3...d5 4.exd5 exd5 5.d4, a symmetrical position where both sides can end up with isolated d-pawns after cxd4. Black also plays 3...Nf6 4.e5 Nd5 5.d4 cxd4 6.cxd4 for a tenser game. White tries for a stable centre, Black equalises without much risk.

white_ideas.idea: Build the d4-e4 centre and keep a small space edge.
Play Bd3 and O-O and use the e5 or d5 squares.

black_ideas.idea: Hit the centre at once with ...d5 and trade into a symmetrical position.

typical_structures.structure: Symmetrical pawn structure with d4 against d5 after the exchanges, isolated d-pawns on both sides.
Open Sicilian-like asymmetry if White gets e5 and Black plays ...d6.

structure.notes: Symmetrical exchange structure with an open file. Semi-open.

approach.notes: Alapin is standard per the anchors.

sublines_that_differ.name: 3...Nf6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black accepts a space disadvantage for piece activity.

structure.reason: Symmetrical exchange structure with one open file.

approach.reason: Alapin is standard in the anchors.

plans.reason: The 3...d5 line leads to symmetrical IQP positions.
